newsitem.title: USA: Oak Industries says finds irregularities.
newsitem.headline: Oak Industries says finds irregularities.

text.p: Oak Industries Inc said it has discovered accounting irregularities within its OakGrisgby Inc unit, allegedly committed by the division's controller.

Oak alleged that during an audit of its 1996 financial statements, it found that the controller, who was not identified, "in collusion with two of his assistants, capitalized certain amounts which should have been expensed..."
Revenues for the periods involved were not affected, Oak said.

Oak said the amounts, totalling $3.5 million ($2.2 million after taxes), related to 1995 and the first three quarters of 1996. Oak said the first, second and third quarters of 1996 have been restated and the cumulative effect of the 1995 misstatements is reflected in the restated financial statements for the three months ended March 31, 1996.
Because the impact on 1995 was not material, the 1995 financial statements were not restated.
Oak said outside legal counsel and independent accountants conducted an investigation, and "confirmed that the accounting irregularities were isolated to this one division."
Oak said it fired all three employees, and filed suit against them. Details about the suit were not immediately available.

"Although the amounts involved were not material to Oak's overall operating results during the periods in which the expenses were incurred, we are outraged that individuals in positions of trust would violate their fiduciary responsibility by acting in this manner," said William Antle, chairman and chief executive officer. "Oak will not tolerate such a complete disregard of its ethical standards by any individual."
OakGrigsby produces traditional analog and digitial switch controls, and is based in Sugar Grove, Ill.
Oak Industries is a supplier of components to manufacturers and service providers in the communications industry.
